newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded differentials down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded differentials down.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials drifted lower on Wednesday in the Group Three spot market in another day of thin trade, traders said.
Discussion this week has been muted as traders attended the National Petroleum Refiners Association annual conference in San Antonio, but the pace was expected to pick up later today.
"It's been really quiet. Even the floor has been quiet," one trader said.
Group Three unleaded gasoline was bid 3.75 cents a gallon under NYMEX April unleaded, down one cent on the day following a rally in NYMEX front-month unleaded.

Winter-grade unleaded in Chicago firmed to bids 8.75 cents a gallon under the print with few deals heard done, while summer-grade barrels were talked 3 cents a gallon under the print. The seasonal change in gasoline grades occurs in April.
Low sulphur diesel for prompt deliveries eased to bids 3.50 cents a gallon over NYMEX April heating oil in Group Three and were steady at 3.75 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago, traders said.

High sulphur diesel also faded against higher NYMEX heating oil prices, falling to bids 1.50 cents a gallon over the print in Group Three and 2.0 cents over in Chicago for all March timings, traders said.
